data.name: Help_AccountType_Text
data.value: Choose the type that matches what you are tracking. Cash, checking and savings track money you hold. Use credit card for spending you repay later; a debit card belongs to its bank account. A loan tracks money you owe, and money lent tracks what others owe you. An asset account tracks an estimated value, such as a car. Money owed to you and asset values are not cash available to spend.

data.name: Help_AccountType_Example
data.value: An unpaid credit card purchase of 300 gives a card balance of −300. A car valued at 9,000 is recorded as an asset, not as 9,000 available for shopping.

data.name: Help_OpeningBalance_Text
data.value: Enter the money in the account at the start of the selected day, before that day’s transactions. This is the day you start tracking in Zanance, not necessarily the day the bank account was opened. Zanance calculates the balance from this amount and transactions dated that day or later. Do not include the same transaction both in the opening balance and again as a transaction.

data.name: Help_OpeningBalance_Example
data.value: The account had 1,000 at the start of today. You then spent 50. Enter 1,000 as the opening balance and record the 50 expense; Zanance shows 950.

data.name: Help_OpeningUnknown_Text
data.value: Choose this when you do not know the opening balance. You can start recording transactions without guessing. Zanance uses zero temporarily and marks the balance as incomplete; this does not mean the account really had no money. Later, enter the correct opening balance or compare the recorded balance with the actual balance in the account details.

data.name: Help_ReportCurrency_Text
data.value: Choose the currency used to show a combined value for accounts in different currencies. Zanance converts the totals using the exchange rates you enter. It does not exchange money or change any account’s currency or recorded transactions. If a required rate is missing, the combined total is incomplete. The original totals in each currency remain available.

data.name: Help_ReportCurrency_Example
data.value: You have 100 EUR and 100 USD. With an example rate of 1 USD = 0.90 EUR, the combined value is 190 EUR. Your accounts still contain 100 EUR and 100 USD.

data.name: Help_MonthStartDay_Text
data.value: Choose the day that starts your monthly tracking period. Use the first day for a calendar month, or another day to match when you usually receive your income. Monthly budgets, Home, reports and monthly transaction filters use this period. This does not change transaction dates, scheduled payment dates or weekly budget periods.

data.name: Help_MonthStartDay_Example
data.value: With the Gregorian calendar and a start day of 25, the September period runs from September 25 through October 24. A bill due on October 1 is still due on October 1.

data.name: Help_Mode_Text
data.value: Choose how many options you want to see. Simple keeps everyday tasks prominent. Advanced shows extra controls for detailed budgeting, account selection and contracts. Both modes use the same records and calculations. Returning to Simple does not delete your data or turn off options you have already set; relevant advanced settings are summarized.

data.name: Help_AppLock_Text
data.value: Turn this on to require your device’s unlock method when opening Zanance, and again after being away for at least 30 seconds. Depending on your device, this may use a fingerprint, face recognition or device PIN. App lock restricts access to the app; it does not by itself encrypt your financial files. Backup passwords are separate.

data.name: Help_NotificationDetails_Text
data.value: Turn this on to let reminders include financial names and amounts. Leave it off for general reminders without those details; reminders are not disabled. Your device settings decide whether notifications appear on the lock screen. When details are enabled, anyone who can see the notification may also see that information.

data.name: Help_NotificationDetails_Example
data.value: With details off, a reminder does not show the payment name or amount. With details on, it can show that rent of 900 EUR is due.

data.name: Help_AmountMode_Text
data.value: Choose how certain the planned amount is. Fixed: you know the amount and expect it to stay the same. Estimated: enter your best estimate; forecasts identify it as approximate. Unknown: leave the amount undecided until you know it. Forecasts stay incomplete rather than counting it as zero. When recording the actual payment, use the amount really paid or received.

data.name: Help_WeekendRule_Text
data.value: Choose what Zanance should do when a scheduled date falls on one of your configured weekend days: keep the date, move it to the previous working day, or move it to the next one. Supported public holidays count only when that option is enabled. Only the date in Zanance changes; this does not reschedule a bank payment or change a contract.

data.name: Help_WeekendRule_Example
data.value: If Saturday and Sunday are non-working days in your settings, moving a Sunday payment to the next working day puts it on Monday, unless an enabled holiday rule excludes Monday too.

data.name: Help_AutoPost_Text
data.value: For a fixed-amount plan, this creates the scheduled transaction when you next open Zanance on or after its due date. The transaction is marked for review. It records what was planned; it does not check your bank, pay a bill or transfer money. Check the amount and date before confirming it. Do not also enter the same payment separately.

data.name: Help_AutoPost_Example
data.value: You plan rent of 900 for the first of each month. Opening Zanance on the second creates a 900 expense to review. It does not send 900 to your landlord.

data.name: Help_PlanApplyFrom_Text
data.value: Choose the first date from which the new plan settings should apply. Earlier scheduled items keep their previous amounts and dates. Use this when a regular payment changes without rewriting earlier months. This setting changes the plan in Zanance; it does not change your contract or payment instructions at the bank.

data.name: Help_PlanApplyFrom_Example
data.value: Rent rises from 900 to 950 in March. Apply the change from March 1: January and February keep 900; scheduled payments from March use 950.

data.name: Help_Reimbursable_Text
data.value: Use this for an expense you paid but expect someone else to repay, in full or in part. Enter who owes you and the amount you expect back. The amount remains outstanding until you record the money received. Record it against the original expense as a refund, not as new income, so your net spending is reduced correctly.

data.name: Help_Reimbursable_Example
data.value: You pay 60 for a shared meal and a friend owes you 20. Record the 60 expense and 20 expected back. When you record receiving the 20, your net cost is 40.

data.name: Help_ForeignAmount_Text
data.value: Use this when the receipt is in a different currency from the account charged. The main transaction amount must be the amount actually deducted, in the account’s currency. Store the receipt’s currency and amount as the original amount. It is extra information, not a second expense, and it does not replace the amount shown by your bank.

data.name: Help_ForeignAmount_Example
data.value: A receipt shows 100 USD, while your euro account is charged 92 EUR. Record an expense of 92 EUR and an original amount of 100 USD. Do not also record another expense of 100.

data.name: Help_SpendingType_Text
data.value: This classifies a category for a Flex budget. Fixed: regular monthly bills, such as rent. Non-monthly: bills paid less often, such as an annual insurance bill; a monthly equivalent is shown for planning. Flexible: everyday spending covered by your shared flexible limit. The classification does not create a payment or put money aside.

data.name: Help_SpendingType_Example
data.value: An annual insurance bill of 600 belongs under Non-monthly. Its monthly planning share is 50. This does not create twelve payments or reserve 50 in your bank account.

data.name: Help_BudgetMethod_Text
data.value: Choose how to plan spending. Spending limits: set a maximum for the period and, optionally, for categories. Envelopes: divide money you already have among categories and see what is still unassigned. Flex: track monthly bills and the monthly share of less frequent bills separately; use one limit for everyday spending. Envelopes and Flex are monthly methods. These are tracking tools: they do not move money or block bank payments.

data.name: Help_BudgetMethod_Example
data.value: Suppose you have 1,000, with nothing already reserved for goals. Assigning 600 to envelopes leaves 400 unassigned. The 600 is planned spending, not an expense that has already happened.

data.name: Help_Rollover_Text
data.value: Choose what happens to unused budget at the next period. Start fresh uses only the new limit. Carry over unused budget adds the previous period’s remaining allowance. Carry over both also subtracts any overspending. The calculation follows consecutive budgets and stops at a gap. It changes the spending allowance, not your bank balance or the money assigned to goals.

data.name: Help_Rollover_Example
data.value: Suppose each period has a base limit of 500. Spending 450 leaves 50 to carry over, making the next limit 550. Spending 560 instead makes it 440 if carrying over overspending is enabled.

data.name: Help_BudgetPeriod_Text
data.value: Choose whether this budget covers a month, one week or 14 days. Weekly and two-week budgets use spending limits; Envelopes and Flex are available for monthly budgets. Each period has its own limit. A weekly budget does not divide or replace your monthly budget. The same expense can appear in both views, so do not add their spending totals together.

data.name: Help_BudgetPeriod_Example
data.value: You can have a weekly grocery limit of 100 and a separate monthly grocery limit of 400. A grocery purchase of 20 uses 20 of each relevant limit, but it is still just one 20 expense.

data.name: Help_FortnightStart_Text
data.value: Choose the first day of a two-week budget period. Every period lasts exactly 14 days, and the next starts immediately after it. Pick a payday if you want the budget to follow a two-week pay cycle. This is not the same as splitting each month into two halves; period boundaries can move across calendar months.

data.name: Help_FortnightStart_Example

data.name: Help_BackupPassword_Text
data.value: Password protection encrypts local and cloud backup files. You can reuse the same password, but must enter and confirm it each time; Zanance never saves it. Restoring an encrypted file needs its original password, even on another device. Keep it safe: the developer cannot recover it and your device PIN cannot replace it. You can turn protection off; anyone who obtains an unencrypted file can read its contents, even if it was stored in your own cloud account.

data.value: Before a restore replaces the current profile’s data, Zanance makes a safety copy on this device. It keeps only recent copies in the app’s private storage; these safety copies are not encrypted. They are not a substitute for a password-protected backup kept elsewhere.
